A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Q-UCRL for infinite-horizon average-reward MDPs. Their complete text, equations, algorithm displays, Figure 1, and Appendices A–B support comparison despite substantial reformatting and revisions to the quantum estimator.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical bounds and proofs, with supplementary mathematical and background material in the appendices. It contains no original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. Its 'quantum experiments' describe oracle operations and analytical query complexity, not reported experimental outcomes.

M1.justification: v2 uses separate binary transition-indicator oracles and the scalar SubGaussEst estimator. v3 replaces these with a superposition over next states and the multivariate QBounded estimator, supplied as Algorithm 1. This changes the central quantum inputs and estimation procedure, while retaining optimistic policy optimization and weighted averaging across epochs.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets, benchmarks, or instantiated test environments. The revised theoretical oracle model does not constitute added empirical task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Classical RL algorithms and regret bounds are discussed as theoretical context.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol. Changes to quantum query budgets specify the proposed algorithm, rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies. Appendices A–B retain the convexity argument and amplitude-amplification overview.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, measured uncertainty, or significance tests. Revisions to probabilistic estimator guarantees belong to the theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: No measured result values, rankings, or qualitative evaluation findings are added or revised. The changed analytical regret guarantee is assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Definitions 2–3 revise the quantum-access formalism, and Lemmas 1–4 replace scalar variance-dependent estimation bounds with multivariate bounded-variable guarantees and revised derivations. Theorem 1 retains the S^5 A^4 T_mix prefactor but replaces log^(11/2)(S^2AT) log log(T) with log^3(T/(SA)) log^(1/2)(T sqrt(S)) log(S^2AT). The MDP assumptions and appendix arguments remain.

C1.justification: Contribution 2 changes from outperforming a classical tilde O(sqrt(T)) benchmark to explicitly breaking a classical Omega(sqrt(T)) lower bound. The central tilde O(1) claim and claimed novelty for infinite-horizon average-reward quantum RL remain.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the quantum-estimation explanation for speedups, the martingale-free analysis motivation, and the state-collapse rationale. The limitation to model-based methods and proposed model-free future work are unchanged; added epoch-measurement reminders largely restate v2's procedure.

D1.justification: v3 provides detailed QBounded pseudocode, specifies L2 = 1 and epsilon = 1/25, and explicitly converts epoch visit counts into the estimator parameter in Eq. (25). v2 only invokes the scalar estimator and states its query complexity. These are localized additions to algorithm specification.

R1.justification: v3 adds Cornelissen, Hamoudi, and Jerbi (2022) as the multivariate estimator source and removes Sidford and Zhang (2023). It also changes its description of Ganguly et al. (2023) from an adopted interaction framework to neighboring finite-horizon work. Most related-work positioning remains.

P1.justification: The section sequence and much of the prose remain. Targeted rewrites explain the revised quantum foundations and estimator, with added notation explanations, an epoch-policy remark, and an equal-contribution note. Citations change from numerical to author–year style.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout from two columns to one, with wider equations, different typography, and running headers. Figure 1 is enlarged and its quantum-state label updated. A new estimator algorithm display is added, and existing algorithms, derivations, references, and appendices are extensively reflowed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's external estimator call, v3 provides more inspectable pseudocode and parameter choices and reports tighter logarithmic dependence. However, new Algorithm 1, lines 7 and 9, prints a normalization factor of 1/sqrt(md/2) for sums over m^d states, which does not generally normalize them. Whether this is merely a transcription error is unresolved. The documentation gains and new correctness concern prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
